data.title: Top Salon Scheduling Software Compared Features, Pricing and Costs
data.ai_summary: Eight salon scheduling platforms are compared, covering Bookeo, Mangomint, Boulevard, GlossGenius, Fresha, Vagaro, Square Appointments, and Acuity Scheduling. Pricing models vary from flat tiers to per-user fees and marketplace commissions, with tradeoffs noted for each. The comparison highlights how cost structures differ across platforms.

industries.name: Personal Care & Wellness Booking Platforms (Beauty, Fitness, Spa)

data.full_text:
Home Press Release Top Salon Scheduling Software Compared: Features, Pricing And Key Differences

Top Salon Scheduling Software Compared: Features, Pricing and Key Differences Published: 29 Sep 2026 Author: Precedence Research Share: Top Scheduling Software Compared: Head-to-Head Feature Breakdown If you run a salon or a day spa and you are shopping for scheduling software right now, the hard part is not finding options. There are dozens, and most of them will take a booking, send a reminder, and hold a card. The hard part is that the platforms are priced on completely different logic, so two systems that look almost identical on a feature grid can be several thousand dollars apart over a year, depending on how many chairs you have and where your new clients come from. This is a large and growing trade, which is part of why the software market around it is so crowded. Federal labor projections have employment of barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists growing 7 percent between 2025 and 2035, off a base of roughly 670,800 jobs. We compared eight platforms that salon and spa owners actually shortlist, and we have written every entry to the same template so the comparison is like-for-like. How This Comparison Was Put Together We started from the pages that currently rank for salon and spa scheduling queries and pulled out every vendor that appeared on more than one of them, then removed the tools that are general-purpose calendar apps with a beauty landing page attached. What was left is the eight platforms below. For each one we did the same three things. We opened the vendor's own pricing page and recorded the published numbers, including per-user charges, per-location charges and card processing rates, because those are the figures that move the annual total. We recorded the current Capterra rating and the review count, as plain text, so you can see how much evidence sits behind each score. Then we identified one limitation for every platform, including the one we placed first. We did not accept "contact us for pricing" as an answer, and no vendor paid for placement or for a particular position in the list. Ratings and prices were checked in September 2026 and they do change, so treat them as a starting point rather than a quote. The Eight Platforms At A Glance Platform Starting price Pricing model Best for Main tradeoff Capterra rating Bookeo $14.95 a month Flat tiers by staff count and booking volume Salons and spas that want a predictable bill Branches run as separate accounts 4.3 (103 reviews) Mangomint $130 a month Base fee plus per user Salons with a front desk and a full service menu High cost floor for very small teams 5.0 (344 reviews) Boulevard $140 a month per location Tiered per location Multi-location salons, spas and medspas Priced per location, entry tier caps professionals 4.6 (389 reviews) GlossGenius $24 a month Flat tiers, payments included Solo stylists and small teams Rooms, waivers and waitlist sit on higher tiers 4.8 (349 reviews) Fresha $19.95 a month Subscription plus new-client commission Salons that want marketplace demand 20 percent commission on new marketplace clients 4.8 (1,447 reviews) Vagaro $30 a month Scales with bookable calendars Mixed beauty and wellness businesses Marketing tools and branded app excluded from trial 4.7 (3,651 reviews) Square Appointments $0 a month Free tier, then per location Salons already on Square hardware No-show fees and waitlist require a paid plan 4.5 (260 reviews) Acuity Scheduling $16 a month Tiered by number of calendars Single-service providers and small studios A scheduler rather than a salon system 4.8 (5,758 reviews) 1. Bookeo Best for: salons and spas that want a predictable flat monthly bill and industry-specific scheduling rather than a percentage of every booking. If you are comparing these eight platforms on cost, this is the one where the pricing structure is the main argument. Bookeo prices on staff count and on monthly booking volume, so the bill does not move when you have a good month, and the software vendor does not take a commission out of a booking; card processing runs through Stripe, Square, or PayPal at those providers' own published rates. The appointments product is also one of three separate products (the other two are built for classes and for tours and activities), which is a different design decision from the single general-purpose system that most of this category ships. Key features Real-time booking through a widget embedded in your existing site, or a standalone branded booking page if you do not have one

Staff assigned to specific services with working hours set per staff member and per location, plus calendar sync with Google Calendar, iCal, Outlook and Office 365

Deposits, full prepayment or a card held on file, with automatic email and text reminders and online rescheduling

Client database with intake forms, prepaid packages, memberships and gift vouchers, and digital waivers as a paid add-on Pricing: five tiers, quoted on the US pricing page as Solo at $14.95, Small at $29.95, Standard at $39.95, Large at $79.95, and X-Large at $119.95 a month. The tiers run from 1 consultant and 200 bookings a month up to 60 consultants and 3,000 bookings a month. Digital waivers are an add-on at $9 to $249 a month depending on volume, and text credits are $0.09 each. The free trial is 30 days with no credit card required. Rating: 4.3 on Capterra from 103 reviews. Where it falls short: multi-branch businesses are handled through a portal in which customers search for a branch or centre and then book with that individual branch, and each branch is a standalone account that controls its own schedule, staff, customer database, sales reports and statistics. Data is not shared between branches. Each branch has its own customers, its own members and its own gift vouchers, so a voucher bought at one branch can only be redeemed at that branch. The portal manager can go into each sub-account's backend and pull portal reports (booking summaries and a revenue summary) for each sub-account, but if you are expecting one combined customer list across five sites, that is not the model. The review base is also small next to the platforms further down this list, which is worth knowing when you are reading scores. 2. Mangomint Best for: salons and spas with a front desk and a full-service menu that want one system running the floor rather than a calendar and a till kept separately. Mangomint is built on the assumption that you have a front desk and somebody standing at it. Pricing is $120 a month as a base fee plus $10 per user, so the smallest realistic monthly bill is $130, and the bill rises with headcount rather than with bookings. What you get for that is a system intended to run the whole floor rather than only the calendar, which includes point of sale, retail and inventory, forms and charting, and staff management. Key features Calendar, online booking, Express Booking and a virtual waiting room for walk-ins and gaps

Point of sale with retail and inventory, gift cards, memberships and packages

Forms and charting, client management and web chat

Staff management, reporting and multi-location support in the base plan Pricing: $120 a month base plus $10 per user, with additional locations at $120 a month each. Add-ons are priced separately, including phone at $70 a month per line, marketing from $30 a month, and payroll at $50 a month plus $8 per worker. Card processing is 2.45 percent plus 15 cents in person and 2.90 percent plus 30 cents for virtual transactions. A free trial account is available. Rating: 5.0 on Capterra from 344 reviews. Where it falls short: the cost floor. A three-stylist salon is at $150 a month before a single add-on, and a solo operator is paying for a front-desk system that will not be used. The reporting and inventory depth is real, but it is depth you have to be big enough to need. 3. Boulevard Best for: multi-location salons, spas and medspas that need per-location control, per-location reporting and treatment-side depth. Boulevard is priced and reported per location, and that is the design assumption underneath the whole product rather than an option that has been added on afterwards. The tiers escalate on the number of professionals and on the volume of texts and email blasts included. It appears on medspa shortlists about as often as it appears on salon shortlists, which is a reasonable signal about where the product depth actually sits. Key features Per-location scheduling, reporting, and staff permissions

Client messaging with included text and email allowances that scale by tier

Forms as a paid add-on for intake and consent, which matters for treatment-led businesses

Integrations including QuickBooks as a paid add-on Pricing: Essentials is $176 a month per location, or $140 with annual billing, and covers up to 5 professionals with 100 texts, 500 email blasts, and 25 GB of storage. Premier is $293, or $234 annually, and lifts that to unlimited professionals, 250 texts, and 1,000 email blasts. Prestige is $410, or $328 annually, and adds the forms add-on with 2,500 texts and 10,000 email blasts. Enterprise pricing is quoted on request. Forms is $65 a month; QuickBooks is $45 a month. Rating: 4.6 on Capterra from 389 reviews. Where it falls short: the price. Two locations on Essentials is $280 a month at least, and the entry tier stops at 5 professionals, which many two-site salons will pass quickly. Card processing rates are not published on the pricing page, so you will have to ask for them before you can compare the real cost against the platforms that do publish. 4. GlossGenius Best for: solo stylists and small teams that want one flat price with card processing included in it. Solo stylists and small teams are the audience here, and the pricing reflects that. The Standard plan is $24 a month billed annually and includes the booking site, client notifications, email and text marketing, inventory and retail, and packages and memberships, with card processing at a flat 2.6 percent. For a one-chair business, that is a straightforward number to plan against. Key features Custom booking website with unlimited client notifications

Email and text marketing included from the entry plan

Inventory, retail, packages and memberships

Forms and waivers, Google booking, automated waitlist, and room and resource management from the Gold plan Pricing: Standard is $24 a month, Gold is $48 a month, and Platinum is $148 a month, all billed annually. Medspa plans are separate at $148 and $248 a month. Card processing is a flat 2.6 percent with no extra charge for tap-to-pay or card on file; instant payouts cost 1.8 percent, and the payroll add-on is $40 a month plus $6 a seat. The free trial is 14 days with no credit card. Rating: 4.8 on Capterra from 349 reviews. Where it falls short: the features a spa needs are not on the cheap plan. Room and resource management, automated waitlist, and forms and waivers all start on Gold at $48 a month, which is double the headline price. If you are a hair salon, the Standard plan may well be enough; if you have treatment rooms, it probably is not. 5. Fresha Best for: salons that want marketplace demand and are willing to pay a commission for the new clients that marketplace sends them. With Fresha, the subscription price is not the figure that decides what you pay in a year. Fresha charges $19.95 a month for an independent professional and $14.95 per team member per month for a team, which is genuinely low, and it then takes a 20 percent one-time commission on every new client who books through the Fresha marketplace, with a minimum fee of $6 per client, while returning clients are free. That commission is a customer acquisition channel with a price attached to it, and our view is that it gets misread as free software more often than any other pricing arrangement in this category. Key features Marketplace exposure to consumers searching for salons in your area

Subscription priced per team member rather than per location

Card processing built in, with buy now pay later available through Klarna

Optional add-ons for loyalty, insights, review generation, and an AI concierge Pricing: Independent is $19.95 a month, Team is $14.95 per team member a month, and enterprise pricing is quoted on request. The new-client marketplace commission is 20 percent with a $6 minimum per client. Online card payments are 2.79 percent plus $0.20; in-person payments are 2.29 percent plus $0.20 with an extra 10 cents for tap-to-pay, and manual card entry is 3.30 percent plus $0.20. Add-ons include client loyalty at $59.95 a month per location, insights at $9.95 per bookable team member, and an AI concierge at $99.95 a month per location. Rating: 4.8 on Capterra from 1,447 reviews. Where it falls short: the commission is charged on new clients, which means the cost of the platform rises exactly when the business is growing. If most of your new bookings already come from your own site, your own social accounts or word of mouth, you are paying a marketplace rate for demand you generated yourself, and you should model that before you switch. 6. Vagaro Best for: mixed beauty and wellness businesses where several different kinds of providers share one roof and one booking system. Vagaro has been in this market a long time, and it shows in the breadth of the feature list and in the size of the review base, which is over 3,600 on Capterra. The entry price is low and the platform scales by the number of bookable calendars rather than by location, which suits mixed businesses where hair, nails, massage and fitness share a roof. Key features Booking, calendars and client records for beauty, wellness and fitness businesses in one system

Website builder, marketing tools and a branded client app available in the subscription

Merchant services with a card reader included on sign-up

Pricing tiers selected by the number of bookable calendars, from one up to seven or more Pricing: the published rate is $23.99 a month as an introductory price for the first six months, with a standard price of $30.00, and the plan cost rises as you add bookable calendars. The free trial is 30 days and covers all features except email marketing, text marketing and the branded app. Card processing rates are quoted through Vagaro merchant services rather than published on the pricing page. Rating: 4.7 on Capterra from 3,651 reviews. Where it falls short: the trial excludes email marketing, text marketing and the branded app, which are three of the things a salon is most likely to be evaluating. You can trial the calendar but not the growth tools, so the first real test of those happens after you are already paying. 7. Square Appointments Best for: salons that already take payment on Square hardware and want the booking calendar attached to the till. There is a free tier here, and for a solo stylist who already takes payments on Square hardware it is a reasonable place to start, because booking is attached to the till and the reporting is one system rather than two. The paid tiers are priced per location and they also buy down the card processing rate, which is unusual and worth doing the arithmetic on if your card volume is high. Key features Online booking site, integrations, appointment reminders and unlimited staff calendars on the free plan

Cancellation policy, no-show fees, multi-staff appointment booking and a waitlist on the Plus plan

Future bookings report, service cost tracking and resource management on the Premium plan

Booking, payments, and reporting in one account with Square point of sale Pricing: Square Free is $0 a month, Square Plus is $49 a month per location, and Square Premium is $149 a month per location. In-person card processing is 2.6 percent plus 15 cents on Free, 2.5 percent plus 15 cents on Plus, and 2.4 percent plus 15 cents on Premium. Online payments are 3.3 percent plus 30 cents on Free and 2.9 percent plus 30 cents on the paid plans. Paid plans include a trial period. Rating: 4.5 on Capterra from 260 reviews. Where it falls short: the free plan is thin in the places where salons actually lose money. Cancellation policies, no-show fees, and the waitlist all require Plus at $49 a month per location. Payment processing is also Square-only, so if you have a processing rate you like elsewhere, you cannot bring it with you. 8. Acuity Scheduling Best for: single-service providers, mobile therapists, and small studios that need a scheduler rather than a salon management system. Acuity Scheduling is a scheduling tool that a lot of beauty professionals use, rather than a salon management system that happens to schedule. It is owned by Squarespace; the calendar and intake side is well built, and it is priced by the number of calendars you need rather than by staff or by location. For a single-service provider, a small studio or a mobile therapist, that is often the right shape. Key features Client self-scheduling with unlimited services and appointments on every plan

Payments through Stripe, Square, PayPal, and Venmo

SMS reminders, packages, and gift certificates from the Standard plan

HIPAA business associate agreement and custom API and CSS access on Premium Pricing: Starter is $16 a month billed annually or $20 monthly and includes 1 calendar. Standard is $27 annually or $34 monthly and includes up to 6 calendars. Premium is $49 annually or $61 monthly and includes up to 36 calendars. The free trial is 7 days and does not require a credit card. Rating: 4.8 on Capterra from 5,758 reviews. Where it falls short: it is a scheduler, and the salon-specific layer is not the centre of the product. There is no retail-first design, and the trial is only 7 days, which is short if you intend to import a client list, build a service menu, and test a real week of bookings before you decide. What to compare besides the booking calendar Most feature grids in this category compare the same eight things, and most of those eight are now table stakes. These are the areas where the platforms above genuinely differ. Online booking and per-staff calendars Every platform here will publish availability and take a booking. What varies is whether the system understands that a service is tied to a specific person with specific hours, that some services can only be performed by some staff, and that two stylists cannot occupy the same station. If you have more than two people, ask to see double-booking prevention configured, not described. Deposits, Cancellation Windows and No-Show Fees This is the group of settings that has money directly attached to it, and it is the group where the detail is worth checking carefully. A workable configuration will let you require a deposit or full prepayment on selected services, hold a card on file for the rest, define a cancellation window, and then charge the fee automatically when somebody cancels inside that window. Note that once you store a card to charge a late-cancellation fee later, you are handling payment account data. The standards for that are set by the card industry's security council, which was founded in 2006 by the major payment brands, and compliance is a question you should be asking your software vendor rather than assuming. Client Self-Service: Rescheduling, Cancelling And The Waitlist Self-service is the feature that removes phone calls, and it has two halves. The first is that a client can move or cancel a booking from the confirmation email or a client area without calling the salon. The second is that when a slot is released, the system automatically offers it to a waitlist rather than leaving a hole in the day. Plenty of platforms do the first. Fewer do the second, and on some of them the automated waitlist sits on a higher tier, so check which plan it is on before you price the system. Memberships, Packages And Gift Vouchers If you sell a six-session package or a monthly membership, the software has to track the balance, the expiry and the recurring charge, and it has to do that at the point of booking rather than in a spreadsheet afterwards. Gift vouchers are a separate question again, particularly for multi-site businesses, because the rules about where a voucher can be redeemed differ by platform. The Layer Beyond Booking: Point Of Sale, Retail And Staff Commission For a hair salon with a retail shelf and a commission structure, the booking calendar is maybe half the job. Point of sale, inventory, and commission tracking on both services and product sales are the parts that decide whether you are running one system or three. Mangomint and Boulevard are built with that layer in mind; the lower-priced schedulers generally are not, and that is a fair reason for the price gap. Client Apps And Staff Apps These are two different things, and they get conflated. A client app is a booking app your customers install, and it is mostly a retention and rebooking tool. A staff app is what your team uses to see their own schedule, check a client note before a service, and take a payment on the floor. Some vendors charge for one or the other, and a branded client app is frequently an add-on rather than an inclusion. Integrations The list to check is short and specific: your calendar (Google, Outlook, iCal or Office 365), your payment processor, your accounting package, and your email marketing tool. If a platform forces its own payment processing, that is not automatically bad, but it does mean the card rate is part of the subscription decision rather than separate from it. The Pricing Model, Which Is Where Most Of The Money Is Three models are in use across the eight platforms above, and they behave very differently as a business grows. A flat tier priced on staff count and booking volume is predictable, and it does not cost you more in a month when trade is good. The second model, a base fee plus a per-user charge, is manageable at three people and gets expensive at twelve, because the per-user line is charged whether or not that person is generating bookings. The third model, a commission on new clients, is inexpensive while you are quiet and increasingly expensive while you are growing, which is the opposite of what most owners assume when they sign up. Salons are small businesses in the statistical sense as well as the everyday one, since by the federal government's own count 99.9 percent of businesses are small, and at that scale a $10 per-user line item is not a rounding error. Build the twelve-month total under each model with your real numbers before you compare feature lists. Solo, Single-Site Or Multi-Location Changes The Answer For a solo stylist or a single mobile therapist, the calendar is the product, and almost everything else is overhead. GlossGenius, Acuity Scheduling, and the free Square Appointments tier all make sense at that size, and paying $130 a month for inventory and payroll you do not use is a poor trade. For a single location with three to ten staff, the decision usually comes down to whether you need the retail and commission layer. If you do, Mangomint and Boulevard are the serious candidates and the cost is justified. If you do not, a flat-tier platform such as Bookeo or a per-calendar platform such as Vagaro will cover the same booking workload for a fraction of the monthly cost. For multi-location businesses, ask one blunt question early: what exactly is shared between sites, and what is not. Some platforms give you one account with several locations inside it and consolidated reporting. Others, including Bookeo with its portal model, run each branch as a separate account with its own customers, staff, reports and vouchers, and give the portal manager access to each sub-account plus per-sub-account portal reports rather than a merged view. Neither approach is wrong. A franchise where each branch is independently owned often prefers the separated model, while a three-site group under one owner usually wants the consolidated one. What causes trouble is buying the first when you assumed the second, so get the vendor to demonstrate it on your own structure before you sign anything. Which One To Pick Naming one overall winner here would be tidy, and it would also be wrong, because the eight platforms are aimed at businesses of quite different sizes. Mangomint and Boulevard are the strongest choices when the business is large enough to need the full operations layer and can carry the monthly cost of it. For solo operators and very small teams, GlossGenius, Acuity Scheduling and the free Square Appointments tier are all sensible starting points. Fresha is a good arrangement if the marketplace is genuinely bringing you clients you would not otherwise have had, and a poor one if it is not, so that is the number to check first. Vagaro sits in the middle and tends to suit mixed beauty and wellness businesses that have several kinds of providers under one roof. If what you want is salon scheduling software with a predictable flat monthly cost, industry-specific booking rather than a general calendar tool, and no commission taken out of your bookings, Bookeo is built for that buyer, with the caveat about branch separation noted above. Whichever way you go, work out the twelve-month total under each pricing model using your own staff count and your own new-client numbers before you compare anything else. The feature lists across these eight platforms are fairly similar to one another. The annual invoices are not.

data.title: Medical Marketing Whiz Announces Partnership With Boulevard to Help Med Spas and Wellness Clinics Streamline Operations
data.ai_summary: Medical Marketing Whiz announced a partnership with Boulevard to give medspas and wellness clinics access to an all-in-one business management platform with partner pricing. Elite Aesthetics, a client, reported a 71% increase in package sales and a 20% increase in pre-booked appointments after switching to Boulevard.
data.full_text:
World Media Directory · RSS · Email Newsletters There were 1,817 press releases posted in the last 24 hours and 487,649 in the last 365 days.

Medical Marketing Whiz Announces Partnership With Boulevard to Help Med Spas and Wellness Clinics Streamline Operations News Provided By Medical Marketing Whiz Share This Article Medical Marketing Whiz and Boulevard's new partnership The collaboration gives medspas and wellness clinics access to an all-in-one business management platform and partner pricing through Medical Marketing Whiz. Not only does Boulevard offer online booking, charting, POS, memberships, and appointment reminders, but it also allows us to track the marketing ROI by integrating into our ClinicWhiz platform.” — Lori Werner, Founder Medical Marketing Whiz



The announcement comes as many aesthetics and wellness clinics look for ways to modernize their operations and reduce the number of disconnected software tools they use to run day-to-day business. Two of the most common questions Medical Marketing Whiz hears from the practices it works with are which booking software is the best fit and which platform is best suited for managing membership programs. This partnership was developed to give clients a clear, vetted answer to both.



Boulevard combines online booking, EMR and charting, payment processing, membership program management, and automated appointment reminders delivered by email and text into one integrated system. The platform also includes newer capabilities designed for the industry, including Buy Now, Pay Later options and integrated e-prescribing (e-Rx) built for medspas and wellness clinics. By bringing these functions together, practices may be able to reduce administrative complexity and manage the client experience more efficiently from a single dashboard.



For clients of Medical Marketing Whiz, the partnership also carries a practical benefit. Because of the collaboration, practices can access partner pricing that is not offered when signing up directly with Boulevard, including 30 percent off Enterprise packages and 20 percent off standard packages. Established aesthetics and wellness brands such as Face Foundrie, Plump Medspa, and Elite Aesthetics use Boulevard to support their operations, and Elite Aesthetics reported a 71 percent increase in package sales and a 20 percent increase in pre-booked appointments after making the switch. Individual results vary from practice to practice.



"Our clients are always asking us what the best payment processing software is and which software is the best for managing memberships. So this partnership with Boulevard is such a great solution. Not only does it offer online booking, EMR/charting, payment processing, membership programs, and appointment reminders into one modern system, it also allows us to track the ROI of our marketing better because it integrates into our ClinicWhiz platform directly," said Lori Werner, Founder of Medical Marketing Whiz.



The integration between Boulevard and Medical Marketing Whiz's ClinicWhiz platform is a central part of the partnership's value for practices focused on measurable growth. When booking and revenue data flow directly into the marketing platform, clinics can gain a clearer view of how their marketing efforts translate into appointments and revenue. This connection is intended to help practice owners make more informed decisions about where to focus their time and marketing budgets, rather than relying on guesswork or manually piecing data together from separate systems.



Medical Marketing Whiz has built its reputation working closely with the aesthetics and wellness community, including medical spas, functional medicine practices, integrative medicine clinics, and related wellness businesses. The agency focuses on strategies tailored to these specialized fields, where practice owners often juggle patient care, compliance considerations, and the operational demands of running a growing business. By evaluating and partnering with platforms already trusted within the industry, Medical Marketing Whiz aims to give its clients access to tools and pricing that support long-term, sustainable growth.



Practices interested in learning more can schedule a call with Marina Downs from the Boulevard team, who can walk clinic owners through the platform and answer questions about how it may fit their operations. Those who reach out are encouraged to mention that they would like the Medical Marketing Whiz discount in order to receive the partner pricing. Additional information is available at



The timing of the announcement aligns with a period in which many aesthetics and wellness clinics are reevaluating their technology stacks and looking for opportunities to consolidate systems, improve the client experience, and better understand their return on marketing investment. For practices that have been considering a change but have been hesitant about the cost or complexity of switching platforms, the partnership pricing and hands-on guidance are intended to make the process more approachable.



As with any business software decision, Medical Marketing Whiz encourages practice owners to evaluate whether a platform fits their specific workflows, patient population, and goals before making a change. The partnership with Boulevard is intended to expand the options available to clients and to provide meaningful savings, not to replace individual due diligence.

Medical Marketing Whiz is a marketing agency dedicated to helping medical spas, aesthetics clinics, and wellness practices grow through strategic marketing, education, and technology partnerships. Founded by Lori Werner, the company works with practices across the country and offers tools such as its ClinicWhiz platform to help clinic owners attract new patients, build recurring revenue, and better understand the results of their marketing efforts. data.full_text:
7月2日，石药集团宣布已与阿斯利康订立合作、选择权及授权协议，以建立战略研发合作，并利用石药集团专有的siRNA药物发现平台和肝外靶向递送平台开发新型小核酸候选药物。本次合作总金额最高达17.7亿美元。
这并非个例，7月1日晚间，君实生物发布公告称，6月30日，公司与复星医药全资子公司复星万邦(江苏)医药集团有限公司签订《授权许可协议》，授权其在大中华地区开发、注册、生产及商业化偌考奇拜单抗(JS005，抗IL-17A单抗)。
根据协议，君实生物将获得2.15亿元不可抵扣且不可退还的首付款，并有资格获得最高达11.25亿元的开发和销售里程碑付款，以及大中华地区净销售额双位数百分比的分级销售提成。
此外，近日，剂泰科技宣布与全球顶级健康投资平台Deerfield Management支持成立的美国生物科技公司Boulevard Bio签署全球独家授权协议，首付款2000万美元，里程碑付款最高达16亿美元。礼来也与信达生物就阿贝西利片在中国大陆的商业化权益达成第八次深度合作。
从传统抗体药物的国内授权，到AI驱动的新药海外授权，再到成熟产品的商业化协同，多笔重磅交易密集落地，为中国创新药BD合作持续升温写下生动注脚。
多元路径并进
君实生物与复星万邦的这笔授权交易，是国内头部创新药企与大型医药集团在自免领域的一次深度协同。偌考奇拜单抗是君实生物自主研发的特异性抗IL-17A单克隆抗体，针对中度至重度斑块状银屑病的Ⅲ期注册临床数据良好，2025年12月新药上市申请已获国家药监局受理。
而复星万邦在自身免疫疾病赛道拥有成熟的商业化团队与完善的市场体系，本次合作能够加快偌考奇拜单抗在大中华地区的研发申报、投产及市场落地速度。
有业内人士指出，2.15亿元的首付款在当前国内授权交易中属于较高水平，这说明市场对JS005的临床价值和商业化前景有充分信心，君实生物选择在NDA阶段引入合作伙伴，也是“研发+商业化”分工协作的理性选择。
另外两笔交易同样值得关注。剂泰科技宣布与全球顶级健康投资平台Deerfield Management取得战略联盟首个重要成果，与Deerfield支持成立的美国生物科技公司Boulevard Bio签署全球独家授权协议，授予其自主研发的三特异性TCE(T细胞衔接器)MTS-128项目在全球范围内的开发、生产及商业化权益。剂泰科技将获得2000万美元首付款，并有资格获得最高达16亿美元的里程碑付款。据公开披露信息，此次交易创下中国制药企业临床前TCE项目单笔海外授权交易金额新纪录，也是中国AI药物递送创新国际化的重要里程碑。
同日，礼来公司与信达生物联合宣布，双方就CDK4&6抑制剂唯择®(阿贝西利片)在中国大陆的权益达成商业化合作协议。根据协议，信达生物将负责该产品在中国大陆的进口、销售、推广和分销;礼来公司将继续作为上市许可持有人，负责生产、供应和持续开发。
值得一提的是，此次合作是双方自2015年建立合作以来的第八次深度合作。阿贝西利是礼来全球核心增长品种之一，根据礼来财报，2025年全球销售额突破57亿美元。米内网数据显示，在国内市场，该产品2025年市场规模已突破11亿元。本次合作与此前双方达成的88亿美元早期靶点全球授权形成互补，共同构建了“海外管线授权引进+国内成熟产品商业化落地”的双向合作格局。
进入“常态化”新阶段
回溯刚刚过去的6月，中国药企BD合作持续活跃。6月1日，海思科宣布与礼来签署《授权与研发合作协议》，双方将在多个疾病领域的创新药物研发开展战略合作。根据协议，海思科将获得最高8700万美元的首付款和近期付款，以及最高29.67亿美元的后续里程碑付款。
同日，云顶新耀宣布与Travere Therapeutics达成独家授权许可与合作协议，授予其EVER001(希布替尼)除大中华区及部分东南亚国家以外区域的独家开发及商业化权益，云顶新耀将获得1.125亿美元的首付款，并有资格获得高达10.3亿美元的里程碑付款。
6月22日，德琪医药宣布与K2 Therapeutics达成两项合作协议，就ATG-106(一款靶向实体瘤的在研CDH6×CD3双特异性T细胞衔接器)授予全球范围(不含大中华区)的独家开发及商业化权利。德琪医药将获得约2000万美元的首付款及近期付款，并有资格获得最高9.605亿美元的里程碑付款。此外，K2还获得一项选择权，可获取德琪医药另一款未披露的双特异性TCE候选药物的全球独家授权。
6月24日，和誉医药宣布与礼来签署战略研发合作与授权协议，双方将围绕多个疾病靶点开展创新药研发合作。和誉医药将获得首付款，并有资格获得最高达19亿美元的里程碑付款。
值得注意的是，公开资料显示，6月22日至24日短短三天内，和誉医药、海思科、英矽智能、德琪医药等多家中国创新药企密集达成海外授权或战略研发合作，潜在交易总金额累计接近90亿美元。
更值得一提的是，合作模式已呈现多元化升级。授权产品从单个项目拓展至多项目打包，合作方式从单向的海外权益许可延伸至共同开发与共同商业化(Co-Co)，部分合作甚至实现“双向授权”，如恒瑞医药与BMS的合作中，恒瑞在向BMS授权的同时，也获得了BMS四个项目在中国大陆及港澳地区的权利，形成了深度绑定的战略协作。
开源证券在近期研报中指出，国内创新药License-out交易保持活跃，我国创新药企业国际合作持续深化，产品出海和全球商业化能力进一步提升。国盛证券研报也认为，中国创新药资产的全球认可度持续提升，出海正从单品种向多技术平台、多疾病领域拓展。
当BD从一次消息逐渐变成一条收入线，当百亿美元级交易从偶发变为日常，中国创新药企的全球化步伐正在持续提速。从抗体、双抗、ADC到AI制药、小核酸、细胞治疗，从肿瘤、自免到代谢、罕见病，中国创新药企正在以多元化的技术路径和合作模式，深度融入全球创新药研发与商业化的产业版图。但BD交易的首付款和里程碑付款往往附带有严格的条件，最终能否全额兑现取决于后续研发和商业化的实际进展，相关风险仍需业界理性看待。

It's a deposit collected at booking, a no-show fee enforced from a card on file, a tip split to the right stylist, retail products added at the counter, and the next appointment booked before the client leaves. The best POS system for salons handles that whole workflow — booking, payments, tips, and retail — without quietly taxing you on processing. This guide compares the seven systems salons and spas ask about most, with real pricing and honest trade-offs. Short on time? How we evaluated Industry stats The salon checkout Comparison table By business type The top 7 The hidden cost FAQ Sources How We Evaluated These Salon and Spa POS Systems We compared 13 salon platforms, booking apps, and POS systems to arrive at these seven finalists. Salons and spas earn revenue by the appointment, which makes their POS needs different from any retail store's — a missed booking is unrecoverable inventory. So every system was scored against the five things that decide whether it actually protects a service business's revenue: Booking and no-show protection — online salon scheduling , deposits at booking, cancellation policies, and no-show fees enforced from a stored card. Empty chairs are the most expensive line item in the industry.

Retail is a second income stream. Product sales routinely add 10%+ to salon revenue — but only when checkout makes adding a product effortless. The takeaway: a salon's POS isn't a cash register. It's the system that protects appointment revenue, keeps stylists' tips clean, and turns checkout into the next booking. Deposits, No-Shows, Tips, and Card-on-File: What Makes Salon Checkout Different A salon POS has to understand the appointment around the payment. Four workflows separate real service business POS systems from generic terminals: Deposits and no-show fees The fix for empty chairs is policy plus tooling: require a deposit or a card at booking for certain services or clients, state the cancellation policy clearly, and let the system enforce it automatically. The critical detail is consent — clients must see and agree to the policy at booking, and the system should record that consent, which is what keeps no-show charges from turning into card disputes. Card-on-file Regulars, memberships, and packages run on stored cards. Cards should only ever be stored tokenized inside the POS or processor — never in a notebook, spreadsheet, or booking note. Done right, card-on-file makes checkout nearly instant and makes recurring revenue (memberships, series packages) possible. Tips and commissions Tip prompts at set percentages raise average tips; tip tracking keeps your team paid correctly. Frequently Asked Questions Salon and Spa POS Questions, Answered What is the best POS system for salons and spas? The best POS system for salons and spas combines online booking with no-show protection, tokenized card-on-file, tip and commission tracking, retail sales, and fair processing rates. For most salons in 2026, Clover configured by Limelight Payments is the strongest overall choice — online booking built into Clover's Services software plans, real hardware, and wholesale rates instead of a locked flat rate. GlossGenius leads for independents who want a salon-first app. Does a salon POS need an appointment booking system? Yes — for an appointment-based business, booking and checkout belong in one workflow. Integrated booking enables deposits at booking, no-show fees from a stored card, automatic reminders, and one-tap rebooking at checkout, which directly protects revenue and retention. How do salons prevent no-shows with a POS system? By requiring a deposit or a card on file at booking, stating the cancellation policy clearly, and letting the system enforce fees automatically. The key detail is recorded consent: when the client agrees to the policy at booking and the system keeps the record, no-show charges hold up against disputes. Can a salon POS track tips and commissions? Yes, and it should. A good salon POS prompts clients with set tip percentages, attributes every tip to the right provider — including split services — and produces per-stylist reports covering tips, services, and product commissions, making payroll a five-minute task. Is it safe to keep client cards on file at a salon? Yes, when cards are stored tokenized inside a PCI-compliant POS or payment processor with the client's recorded consent. Cards should never be written down or stored in booking notes or spreadsheets — that's both a security risk and a compliance violation. How much does a salon POS system cost? Configured by Limelight Payments, it also runs on wholesale rates with hands-on setup and a named advisor. What is spa management software, and is it different from a salon POS? Spa management software emphasizes the service side — intake forms, treatment notes, packages, memberships, and room scheduling — while a POS emphasizes checkout, payments, tips, and retail. Many platforms blend both; the right emphasis depends on whether your complexity lives in the treatment room or at the front desk. Can a salon use a cash discount program to reduce processing fees? Yes — compliant cash discount and dual-pricing programs are increasingly common in salons and barbershops, and can reduce processing costs to near zero. data.title: Worcester names 24 businesses to new legacy program
data.ai_summary: Worcester named 24 businesses to its Legacy Business Program, selected from 62 eligible firms. The businesses have been in operation for an average of 70 years, and honorees will be highlighted at an award ceremony later this year.
data.author: Eric Casey
data.full_text:
The City of Worcester has named 24 businesses to its Legacy Business Program, a designation meant to honor longstanding and influential small businesses.

The recognition will see businesses included in promotional materials and featured on a page on the City’s website. Worcester selected the 24 honorees from a total of 62 eligible businesses nominated by the public, according to a Thursday announcement.

In order to be eligible, businesses are required to have fewer than 250 employees, be physically located in Worcester, be a for-profit, locally-owned firm which is not part of a franchise or chain, and to demonstrate community and cultural significance.

The 24 businesses are:

Sneakerama, 12 Lake Ave.

Addie Lee’s Soul Food, 596 Main St.

Maria’s Kitchen, 826 Main St.

Jo Ann Warren Studio, 997 Millbury St.

Moynagh’s Tavern Inc., 25 Exchange St.

Boulevard Diner, 155 Shrewsbury St.

Ralphs Chadwick Square Diner, 148 Grove St.

Kenmore Diner, 250 Franklin St.

Central Shoe Repair , 37 Mechanic St.

Da-Lat Restaurant, 425 Park Ave.

True Value Hardware , 113 Hamilton St.

Bonardi’s Formalwear , 179 Highland St.

Parkway Diner , 148 Shrewsbury St.

Carlitos Barbershop , 925 Main St.

That’s Entertainment , 244 Park Ave.

Ed Hyder’s Mediterranean Marketplace , 408 Pleasant St.

George’s Coney Island , 158 Southbridge St.

CC Lowell, 455 Pleasant St.

Jerrys Tastee Freeze , 2 Inverness Ave.

Enchanted Fireside , 728 West Boylston St.

Dodge Park Rest Home, 101 Randolph Road

Lou Roc’s Diner, 1074 West Boylston St.

Miss Worcester Diner, 300 Southbridge St.

Marvin’s Corner Lunch , 131 Lamartine St.

ADVERTISEMENT

Winners were scored in partnership with the Museum of Worcester, Preservation Worcester, and the Worcester Regional Chamber of Commerce.

The businesses selected have been in operation for an average of 70 years, according to the City.

Five of the selected restaurants operate from Worcester Lunch Car Co.-produced diners. Worcester Lunch Car Co. manufactured diners from 1906 to 1961, with many still in operation across the North East, according to GBH.

Honorees will be highlighted at an award ceremony to be held later this year.

Eric Casey is the managing editor at Worcester Business Journal, who primarily covers the real estate and banking & finance industries.

Capital’s latest attraction brings millions of flowers and a rare sense of spring to the cityscape

Just opposite Boulevard World, the floral experience is set on 214,000 sq. meters, with 200 million flowers on display and about 2,000 floral sculptures

RIYADH: On a weekday afternoon, Riyadh residents can be seen strolling between flower beds and monuments of sunflowers, dahlias, roses, and lilies — a rare sight in a desert city. But in the Kingdom’s capital, spring sprung when its latest entertainment zone, Boulevard Flowers, opened to the public on April 16, bringing people of all ages and nationalities to discover the colorful and creative designs. A Zimbabwean visitor, Eve Dube, told Arab News: “I didn’t think I would see a lot of Africans here, to my surprise. I’m seeing all nationalities: Africans, Chinese, Filipinos, and I was like ‘Oh my god, I wasn't expecting that. It’s a beautiful gathering of all cultures.” Dube took her friend Clara Garanowako to Boulevard Flowers for her birthday “to enjoy some nature,” she said. She said that it is her first time seeing something like this because there is nothing similar to this scale in Zimbabwe. “I was wowed when I came in, I don't know what to say. This was not what I was expecting … Saudi Arabia is just something else (with) what they did here.” Garanowako added: “I’m really happy, the place is calm, the flowers are blooming. It’s like you connect with nature, which is so nice. I’m so happy!” Just opposite Boulevard World, this floral experience is set on 214,000 sq. meters, with 200 million flowers on display and about 2,000 floral sculptures. These include more than 100 varieties of flowers and plants in 50 different colors set in beds stretching over 8,500 meters. “The place feels like I’m somewhere abroad, like Malaysia, so I’m so pleased that there’s a space like this here,” southerner Hussain Ahmed, who brought his two children Najd and Fazaa along with his wife Sarah to the new experience, told Arab News. “I brought the kids here to have fun, but I wasn’t expecting this …We’re grateful to our leaders who made all of these new experiences possible in Saudi Arabia.” Boulevard Flowers is a unique place to spot different plant species, allow children to learn more at the kids zone, or meet some new friends at the Pet Birds area. Roaa Bandar, 11, told us she felt “so excited” as she walked through the gates to the garden. She was wearing a white and yellow flower crown that she picked at one of the flower kiosks to match her dress. “The place is so beautiful and I want to thank King Salman and the crown prince for making such a place that’s so amazing and refreshing. I really liked it and I hope everyone likes it,” she said. Salem, 13, and 10-year-old Mohammed Aljwaiser, who came to the event with their parents, told us that it was their favorite so far out of the three Boulevard sites. “I felt comfortable as soon as I entered,” Salem said, while Mohammed added: “(When) I first came in, seeing all the flowers was such a nice feeling and the sounds were so relaxing.” The brothers really enjoyed seeing the Saudia Airlines installations that were covered in floral paintings and the ballerina flower sculptures. Salem said he also loved spending time at the Pet Birds section, which features more than 56 types of birds, such as the red-tailed black cockatoo and the Macaw parrots, other unique and rare birds such as the Turaco and Nicobar pigeon, and other rare types such as the flamenco, crowned cranes, and curlews. Visitors can enter for an additional fee to take pictures, hold and play with the birds, or just enjoy the atmosphere. The birds are all trained not to hurt guests. Boulevard Flowers welcomes visitors daily from 4pm to midnight.

data.full_text:
Pipe, a Fintech firm offering embedded financing tools for small businesses, has raised $16 million in a funding round led by investors including Fin Capital and MaC Venture Capital, the company said.

The deal marks Pipe’s first equity fundraising since it relaunched its embedded financing product in 2024, as the company looks to expand partnerships and move closer to profitability.

Marlon Nichols, general managing partner at MaC Venture Capital, has joined Pipe’s board as part of the investment.

Pipe said its financing arm, Pipe Capital, has originated more than 15,000 advances globally over the past two years, with total volume exceeding $300 million.

The company embeds access to working capital within the software platforms used by small businesses, allowing merchants to tap financing without leaving their operating systems.

Its growth has been driven in part by tie-ups with software and payments firms including Boulevard, GoCardless, Housecall Pro, Live Payments and Uber.

Pipe said revenue in the first quarter of 2026 nearly doubled from a year earlier, though it did not disclose absolute figures.

The company has also broadened its reach beyond the United States, with 20% of cumulative capital originations now coming from international markets.

More recently, it signed up AI-powered point-of-sale provider Epos Now to widen access to financing for brick-and-mortar businesses in the United States, Canada, and the UK.

Separately, Pipe said it extended its warehouse facility with Victory Park Capital for two years, for up to $225 million, giving it additional lending capacity as it scales originations.

The raise comes as fintech lenders and embedded finance providers seek to prove they can grow without the cash burn that defined the sector’s earlier expansion.

For Pipe, the pitch to investors appears to rest less on breakout valuation and more on execution: repeat originations, software distribution and tighter capital discipline.

That may resonate in a market where private funding remains selective and investors are rewarding fintechs that can show a clearer path to sustainable earnings rather than growth at any cost.

SAN FRANCISCO--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Pipe, a fintech that provides customer-friendly embedded financial solutions for small businesses, announced a $16 million funding round today, led by investors including Fin Capital and MaC Venture Capital. Through its flagship product, Pipe provides small businesses access to custom capital options in just a few clicks, embedded inside the same tools they’re using to manage their business. For salons that care most about UX and have a team of 2 to 10 staff, Mangomint is a solid choice. For salons that want enterprise-grade operational depth at any size, Zenoti is purpose-built. The six apps reviewed are Sicus Booking (best for AI automation and bilingual support), Fresha (best free option), GlossGenius (best for client experience), Vagaro (best for marketing tools), Boulevard (best for luxury salons), and Square Appointments (best for Square ecosystem users). The guide is published by SICUS Media.
data.author: Sicus Media Inc.

data.ai_summary: This article is a buyer’s guide comparing ten salon booking and management software platforms—Zenoti, Vagaro, Boulevard, Mindbody, Phorest, Fresha, GlossGenius, Square Appointments, Booksy, and Timely—evaluated across twelve criteria including online booking, POS, CRM, and multi-location capability. Published by Zenoti (which also competes in the comparison), the guide recommends different platforms based on business size and needs, from solo operators to multi-location chains. The article includes honest assessments of where Zenoti leads and where it falls short relative to competitors, with pricing ranging from free tiers to custom enterprise quotes.

Zenoti at different business stages — An honest assessment Last updated: May 2026 This guide evaluates ten options for the best booking software for salons across twelve criteria — online booking channels, POS integration, no-show reduction, multi-location management, and more — so you can choose the right platform for where your salon is today and where you plan to be in two years. Most salons switch booking software at least once. Usually because they picked something for where they were rather than where they were going — and by the time they hit the ceiling, they're facing a second migration with an existing client database, a trained team, and no appetite to start over. This guide is designed to help you avoid that. We've covered the full range, from free tools for solo operators to complete management systems for multi-location groups, so you can make the right call for your actual situation — not just your situation today. Before you look at any platform, answer these five questions: How many staff do you currently have?

Are you tracking commissions manually — spreadsheet, calculator, or memory?

Do you operate more than one location, or are you planning to within the next 12 months?

Are clients leaving when stylists leave, rather than staying with the salon?

Is your current booking tool the same one you started with, and are you working around it rather than with it? Your answers matter more than any feature list. If you answered yes to two or more of those questions, pay particular attention to the mid-to-upper range of this comparison. If you answered yes to four or more, skip to the Zenoti section first. Zenoti is the publisher of this article and is included in the comparison — we've noted honestly where it leads and where it falls short, including the things that make it the wrong choice for some businesses. Frequently Asked Questions About Salon Booking Software What is salon booking software? Salon booking software is a digital system that allows salons to manage appointments, enable online client booking, send automated reminders, and connect scheduling to checkout and client management. Modern salon booking software replaces paper appointment books and telephone booking with automated, 24/7 digital systems that reduce no-shows and capture bookings outside business hours. How much does salon booking software cost? Salon booking software costs vary widely — from free plans (Fresha, Square Appointments free tier) to $20–50/month for solo operators (GlossGenius, Timely), $30–175/month for single-location salons (Vagaro, Boulevard), and custom enterprise pricing for multi-location chains (Zenoti, Phorest). Most platforms charge per location, per user, or as a percentage of bookings processed. Factor in transaction fees, hardware costs, and setup fees when comparing total cost of ownership. What is the best free salon booking software? Fresha previously offered a free base plan but has since moved to a subscription model — the Independent plan starts at $19.95/month and the Team plan is $14.95 per staff member per month. Square Appointments still offers a free single-user tier. For salons with an established client base, paid platforms typically become more economical than transaction-fee models above a certain monthly booking volume. Can salon booking software integrate with Google? Yes. Most leading salon booking software platforms — including Zenoti, Vagaro, Boulevard, and Phorest — integrate with Google Reserve, allowing clients to book directly from Google Search and Google Maps results. This is one of the most valuable integrations available because it captures bookings from clients who are actively searching for a salon in their area. What is the difference between salon booking software and salon management software? Salon booking software refers specifically to the appointment scheduling and client booking component. Salon management software is a broader term for an all-in-one platform that includes booking plus POS, CRM, inventory management, marketing automation, and reporting. Most modern platforms — including Zenoti — are full management platforms that include booking as one component of a complete, connected system. When should a growing salon move from a simple booking tool to a full management platform? The clearest signals are operational rather than size-based. If commission reconciliation takes more than 30 minutes a week, if you have no visibility into product costs per service, if clients are leaving with departing stylists rather than staying with the salon, or if you're planning a second location — those are the triggers that make a more complete platform worth the investment and the migration effort. The cost of staying on an outgrown tool tends to be invisible until it compounds: manual workarounds, reporting gaps, and retention problems that are hard to diagnose because the data isn't there. Growing salons that move earlier tend to find the transition less disruptive than those that wait until the pain is acute. Is Zenoti worth it for a single-location salon that is growing? It depends on where your current software is creating friction. Zenoti's value isn't in the feature list, it's in the operational time it removes. Salons that see the clearest ROI are those where commission reconciliation is happening in a spreadsheet, where product costs per service are unknown, or where client retention drops every time a stylist leaves. If those are current problems rather than future concerns, the platform typically pays for itself within 60 to 90 days through recovered missed call revenue, automated rebooking, and the elimination of manual admin. Missed calls, slow responses to website forms or Instagram DMs, and inconsistent follow-up can turn into lost leads and lost potential revenue for your medical aesthetic practice. Automate follow-up using text or email when someone does not book right away or needs reminders. A CRM lets you market smarter, with opportunity to personalize your outreach; you can send the right message to the right patients at the right time, automatically. Manage appointment reminders, reactivation campaigns, and review requests.

Segment patients by treatment interest, birthday month, membership status, or spend level.

Run targeted marketing, for example, a gentle reminder to filler patients who are due for touch ups or to laser patients who are ready for their next series. How to set up simple “journeys” that are triggered by events, consult completed, treatment performed, membership renewal approaching.

How to keep automation feeling personal by using patient names, specific treatment references, and realistic timing. Suggesting subject lines and social captions to speed up your marketing.

Surfacing patterns in your data, like which treatment combinations tend to generate the highest lifetime value. In this guide, we’ll give you the inside scoop on POS software, like what it can actually do for your salon and which are the best POS systems for salons in 2026. What Is a Salon POS System? Salon POS systems are central hubs for the front desk. These software-forward systems support the client experience as much as the salon’s checkout process. They combine software with hardware like iPads and card readers so your clients can easily pay for their visit (and any retail products they’re picking up). A salon POS system is purpose-built for beauty businesses and helps manage payments, appointments, inventory, and client relationships from a single platform. A POS system handles most of your salon’s financial tasks in one place, processing payments, calculating tips and loyalty discounts, and managing retail and reporting programs. Some even make it easy to integrate with other software that tracks staff hours and performance, leading to less manual work on your end. Features To Look for in a Salon POS System Shopping for salon POS software gets a lot easier when you know what to look for. Every self-care business is unique, but here are a few features that most teams need. When comparing salon POS software, prioritize tools that improve both client experiences and day-to-day operations. Fast and flexible checkout: POS software should make paying fast and convenient for everyone, offering things like mobile payment options and easy-to-follow on-screen prompts.

Integrated payments and tipping: Your POS system should support multiple payment options, like mobile wallets and cards on file, so no one has to dig through their wallet for the one method you accept. Look for software that automatically calculates tips at set percentages (like 15%, 20%, and 25%) and applies loyalty rewards and discount codes, too.

Reporting and sales insights: Good salon POS software doesn’t stop working for you once the client has paid. It’ll also include high-level details like retail trends and retention data . These insights can help you adjust your strategies (such as scheduling a full-team workshop to perfect the latest TikTok hairstyle trend) and stay on top of your revenue flow before rent’s due.

Client profiles and purchase history: Choose tools that let you personalize the salon experience. Client profiles store information like their birthdays for special discounts and notes from their past sessions to help your stylists provide better service from moment one.

Retail and inventory management: Keep track of backbar inventory and retail products directly in your POS system. Your software should send an alert when you’re running low and automate order purchasing so you never have to run out of a dye color mid-service. How To Choose the Best Salon POS System Before you start researching and selecting a POS system , you need a game plan. There are lots of software solutions for spas out there, so knowing what you need ahead of time can side-step information overload. These tips will help you stay organized and focus on your salon’s long-term goals. The right POS system for a beauty salon should support your current workflows while giving you room to grow. Define Your Salon’s POS Needs Choosing software starts with taking stock of your needs, so assess your current POS processes. What does the checkout process look like? Where does it slow down? Are there features that overlap with your other software solutions or things you’d like to collapse into one program? Make a list of your wants and needs, then reference it during your search to narrow down your options. Evaluate Ease of Use for Your Staff Your chosen POS software should make your employees’ lives easier. Ideally, they’ll be able to pick it up in their first few days without tons of hands-on training. Part of this onboarding process includes the software company’s customer service, too. A program with a strong team behind it will help you set everything up and get questions answered along the way. Check How the POS Connects To Booking and Scheduling The best POS tools integrate with scheduling systems you already use. Appointment reminders, automated calendar syncing, and easy rebooking options can reduce no-shows and double-booking. This way, your front desk team can schedule clients for a touch-up or a fresh cut in six weeks while they’re still standing at the counter, so they’re more likely to keep coming back . You also need to compare how different software options impact your long-term overhead. Some systems may seem affordable at first, but consider how they’ll impact your overhead over time. Study the fine print: Are there high processing fees? Are their long-term contracts undercut by unreasonable cancellation penalties? POS systems that don’t integrate well with other software means paying for more subscriptions every month, too. Plan for Growth and Scalability You shouldn't have to adjust your business goals around your software or do a massive overhaul every time you outgrow your current system, no matter how big your salon gets. So make sure your beauty salon’s POS has the flexibility to scale with your growing salon. It should be able to manage more locations and team members without glitching, process more complex loyalty and membership programs, and have the wiggle room to add new workflows as tech evolves. 5 Best Salon POS Systems Every POS system has its strengths, but not all of them are going to be the right fit for your needs. Boulevard Blog Medspa • Inspiration Top Medspa Trends for 2026: What’s Hot in Aesthetic Treatments? Top Medspa Trends for 2026: What’s Hot in Aesthetic Treatments? Table of Contents TL;DR

2026 Medspa Trends to Watch

FAQ: 2026 Medspa Trends Jan.15.2026 BY Skya Jones The beauty industry is constantly evolving, and keeping up with what’s new can keep your clients coming back. TL;DR The top medspa trends for 2026 center on personalization, performance, and prevention. AI-powered booking and client insights, regenerative injectables, biostimulators, non-invasive aesthetic treatments, women’s sexual health, IV therapy, GLP-1 weight management, and male aesthetics are reshaping how modern medspas grow revenue and retain clients. Practices that prioritize natural results, holistic wellness, and long-term skin health—supported by smart technology—will lead the next phase of medical aesthetics. 2026 Medspa Trends to Watch AI Is Now Core to the Medspa Client Experience Artificial intelligence has moved from “emerging tech” to essential infrastructure for high-performing medspas. Predictive scheduling and utilization tools reduce downtime and maximize provider availability.

Personalized treatment and product recommendations use client history and behavior to increase retention and lifetime value.

Smarter rebooking and follow-ups help medspas proactively engage clients before demand drops off. Tech that anticipates needs and accelerates growth is now a must-have, not a nice-to-have for medspa operations. For medspa operators in 2026, AI isn’t about automation for its own sake—it’s about delivering a smoother client journey while protecting staff time. From Altering to Restoring: The Shift Toward Natural Beauty Client preferences are moving decisively away from dramatic transformations and toward enhancing what’s already there. Subtle, restorative treatments focus on improving skin quality, symmetry, and tone rather than changing facial structure.

Long-term skin health —including collagen support, hydration, and barrier repair—has become a primary goal.

Preventative aesthetics appeal to younger clients looking to maintain results rather than correct advanced concerns later. In 2026, the most trusted medspas position aesthetics as an investment in confidence and longevity—not reinvention. Regenerative Injectables and Natural Results Take Priority Client expectations around injectables continue to evolve toward biologically driven outcomes. Platelet-rich fibrin (PRF) remains in demand for delicate areas like under-eyes, brows, and perioral lines.

Lower-volume, strategic injections emphasize facial harmony and movement.

Education-led consultations help clients understand why less can often deliver better results. Injectables remain a cornerstone of medspa revenue—but success now depends on restraint, planning, and transparency. Biostimulators as a Key Adjunct in Facial Rejuvenation Biostimulators are increasingly used alongside injectables and energy-based treatments to support collagen regeneration from within. Collagen-stimulating injectables help improve firmness, elasticity, and skin texture over time.

Adjunctive use with PRF, microneedling, and lasers enhances results without over-volumizing.

Gradual, cumulative outcomes align with client demand for natural-looking improvement. In 2026, biostimulators are less about instant gratification and more about future-proofing facial aesthetics. Laser and Energy-Based Treatments Fuel Consistent Growth Non-invasive aesthetic treatments continue to attract clients seeking visible results with minimal downtime. Advanced laser treatments improve texture, tone, and collagen production with faster recovery times.

Multi-modality protocols (laser, RF, injectables) deliver layered results without surgical intervention.

Maintenance-based care plans position lasers as part of long-term skin health—not one-off procedures. Laser technology remains a reliable driver of both client satisfaction and repeat visits in the medspa market. Microneedling Becomes a Precision Skin Strategy Microneedling has evolved into a customizable treatment platform for skin rejuvenation. RF microneedling and depth-controlled devices allow providers to target scarring, laxity, and fine lines more effectively.

Enhanced serums and biologics —including growth factors and PRF—extend results beyond collagen stimulation.

Series-based treatment plans support predictable outcomes and recurring revenue. In 2026, microneedling success is about protocol design, not just the device. Women’s Sexual Health Emerges as a Medspa Wellness Frontier Addressing women’s sexual health is becoming a core component of holistic wellness offerings at medspas—extending beyond aesthetics into quality-of-life care. Sexual wellness goes mainstream , reframing libido, comfort, and vitality as core components of overall health.

Running a successful medical spa today means more than offering injectables or facials—it requires a seamless blend of clinical care, retail efficiency, and spa-level experience. Behind the scenes, your EMR is the backbone that keeps everything running smoothly.

Whether you're launching your first location or scaling a multi-room aesthetics practice, the right EMR empowers you to streamline scheduling, manage inventory, track revenue, and deliver a standout client experience—all while staying compliant.

What is a Med Spa EMR?

A Meds Spa EMR (Electronic Medical Record) is a digital system designed to document and manage clinical, operational, and administrative workflows in a medical spa. Unlike traditional EMRs used in primary care, med spa EMRs are tailored for aesthetics and wellness services—supporting everything from Botox injections and laser treatments to IV therapy and skincare consultations. These platforms often combine scheduling, charting, patient communication, inventory management, and billing in one easy-to-use interface.

Why Use a Med Spa EMR?

Using a medical spa EMR helps streamline daily operations, improve patient experiences, and maintain compliance with medical documentation standards. With features like real-time inventory tracking, automated charting templates, and integrated marketing tools, medspa EMRs can reduce administrative burdens while boosting profitability. Whether you're a solo injector or managing a multi-provider practice with additional services like redlight sauna or cold plunge, the right EMR can help you deliver consistent, high-quality care—and scale your business more efficiently.

Top 9 Medical Spa EMRs

Frequently asked questions What is the best salon management software? There isn’t a single “best” — it depends on your shape. For feature-rich value with robust inventory and purchase orders, many salons pick Vagaro. For small teams and creators who want something beautiful and simple, GlossGenius shines. Use a simple formula: reorder point = average daily usage × lead time (days) + safety stock. Example: you use 5 tubes/day, delivery takes 4 days, and you want 10 tubes of safety stock → 5×4 + 10 = 30. Set minimum at 30 and maximum near 60 so alerts and POs trigger on time. For retail, automate replenishment and track client profiles to recommend the right products. How often should we count inventory — full audits or cycle counts? How do booking and inventory talk to each other? Your booking system should support online booking, appointment booking reminders, and ideally Google Calendarsync. Boulevard Raises $80 Million in Series D Funding to Transform the Client Experience for Self-Care Businesses Share This Article Funding round led by JMI Equity enables Boulevard to accelerate delivery of enterprise capabilities and boost investment in AI research and development to help businesses create more personalized client experiences LOS ANGELES, July 17, 2025-- Boulevard (www.joinblvd.com), provider of the client experience platform purpose-built for appointment-based, self-care businesses, today announced that it has raised $80 million in Series D funding led by JMI Equity, a growth equity firm focused on investments in leading software companies, with continued participation from Index Ventures and VMG Partners. The funding enables Boulevard to accelerate the delivery of enterprise capabilities across multiple self-care verticals while fueling increased investment in AI research and development to help customers continue transforming the client experience through smart technology.



“We’re ecstatic about the opportunity to collaborate with the team at JMI Equity and benefit from their extensive experience helping vertical SaaS companies like Boulevard grow and create generational brands,” said Matt Danna, co-founder and CEO, Boulevard. “In addition to accelerating delivery of the enterprise capabilities customers want today, this new round of funding allows us to pour more resources into discovering and developing the most compelling AI features and building the smartest operational systems possible for these experience-centric businesses. We’re excited to take the self-care industry more fully into the era of AI-powered business growth.”



Boulevard’s boundary-pushing innovations, such as Precision Scheduling™, have already reshaped technology's role in helping self-care businesses deliver seamless client experiences. The game-changing feature on which Boulevard was founded, Precision Scheduling leverages artificial intelligence to analyze booking patterns, appointment durations, and provider availability to suggest the most efficient appointment times. With Precision Scheduling, Boulevard has transformed booking from an arduous, manual, and mostly offline process into a seamless online experience that enables self-care businesses to maximize revenue and exceed the highest of client expectations.



With this new round of funding, the company is positioned to more deeply explore the next generation of intelligence-based technologies for the self-care industry. From using AI to deliver smarter, more customized recommendations for clients, to helping them fine-tune their menu of services and optimize marketing and communications, to developing the most effective packages, promotions, and membership programs possible, Boulevard is poised to help self-care businesses drive greater revenue growth, deliver deeper personalization, and achieve operational excellence.



As part of the Series D investment, Matt Emery, Partner at JMI Equity, has joined Boulevard’s Board of Directors.



“Boulevard is already a clear leader in this fast-growing market, and they’re just getting started,” said Emery. “We’re thrilled to join them on this exciting journey as they continue to transform the client experience in this new era of intelligence-driven technology.”



Fueling growth through innovation



Since its last round of funding in 2022, Boulevard’s revenue has increased by more than 500% as it continues to redefine what’s possible for self-care businesses. Recent enhancements to Boulevard’s platform help customers more seamlessly embed payments into their checkout flow, expand the reach of their commerce and membership programs, and modernize how they market to and communicate with clients.



In addition, as part of its rapid expansion into the fast-growing medspa vertical, Boulevard also launched advanced charting for a more efficient treatment, documentation, and review process, plus technical capabilities, hands-on training, and additional support to help with HIPAA compliance. Less than three years after making its initial foray into the space, Boulevard now powers 15% of the burgeoning U.S. medspa market.



A trusted brand in self-care



Boulevard is now trusted by over 40,000 professionals in more than 5,000 self-care businesses to book more than 2 million monthly appointments and process nearly $5 billion in payments annually. These hair salons, nail salons, medspas, day spas, and barbershops across the U.S. rely on Boulevard for everything from online booking and payment processing to marketing and client communication.



About Boulevard



Boulevard offers the first and only client experience platform purpose-built for appointment-based, self-care businesses. Boulevard empowers business owners and professionals alike to deliver personable, enjoyable experiences to their clients through online appointment scheduling, messaging, marketing, and payments that are simple, elegant, and reliable. Founded in 2016, Boulevard has earned the trust of thousands of salons, spas, medspas, and barbershops across the nation by delivering the world-class technology and genuine, human, personable service they deserve. To learn more, visit joinblvd.com.
